known.title: Disputed keep 6: a choice made on another machine remains in Needs you
A newer shared worker question is hidden and cannot be cleared from a machine with an older question
Not done: publish stuck-worker choice waits
Not done: publish waits from a teammate's worktree
An answered question still prevents work on the asking machine

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 1
Raise: Not done. `is_published` checks only this machine's receipt and event log (`worker.py:359`), so a teammate with a worktree and an existing PR fails this check. Their unanswered worker question is not refreshed to the PR because `worker.py:137` looks up the PR only when answering a question. A stuck-worker choice also refuses here without pushing or refreshing. The same check leaves a size-limit choice on a first close local, although only pre-PR worker questions may remain local. The new tests create these waits on the machine that published the PR, so they miss the handoff.
findings.title: Not done: publish waits from a teammate's worktree

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 1
Raise: Functional. After machine B answers machine A's question and publishes its end, A's local `codex.record` still contains that question. The refusal at `worker.py:116` runs before the new shared-record lookup here, so `forge work <item>` without a note continues to refuse an already answered question. This is a normal handoff that the answer-on-another-machine flow must support.
findings.title: An answered question still prevents work on the asking machine

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 1
Raise: Gate. The supplied proof list names only four `waits` and `stuck-worker` parameterizations. It omits both `blocking-problems` parameterizations in `test_board_needs_you.py` and both new `test_board_blocked.py` parameterizations. The list therefore does not enumerate the required proof for the blocked-plan and Blocked or slow clauses.
findings.title: Not done: proof list

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 1
Raise: Test. The named test never reaches the required state where both machines' Needs you lists are empty: its last assertion explicitly leaves `clash` waiting for a human merge. It also creates the human-merge wait through a new close, so it never proves that an older ready open PR without a wait record appears with `since: null`. Both named cases could break while this test passes.
findings.title: Not done: test_board_needs_you.py

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 1
Raise: Test. The Done-when test explicitly calls for an unfinished item with no visible activity to be absent. This assertion checks a merged old fix and a recently active fix, but creates and checks no unfinished item with `idle_since` null. It would pass if the board incorrectly marked such an item stalled.
